mismatches.say: Rosa gets the hospital bill for her arm. She insures her own car, but the crash was her fault. Who pays?
mismatches.heard: Rosa gets the hospital bill for her arm. She ensures her own car, but the crash was her fault. Who pays?

mismatches.say: Her own policy pays first: Rosa's own P I P pays for her arm.
mismatches.heard: Her own policy pays first. Rose's own PIP pays for her arm.

mismatches.say: Rosa's P I P pays four kinds of benefits. Remember them: Michigan Winters Can Snow.
mismatches.heard: ROSES-P IP pays four kinds of benefits. Remember them, Michigan winters can snow.

mismatches.say: Fifty thousand dollars is only for a named insured on Medicaid, with the household covered.
mismatches.heard: $50,000 is only for named insured on Medicaid, with the household covered.

mismatches.say: No rung at one hundred thousand dollars. No valid choice? You get the sky, unless the premium paid shows another level.
mismatches.heard: No rung at $100,000. No valid choice. You get the sky unless the premium page shows another level.

mismatches.say: Rosa's grandma renews her policy. She and Grandpa, the only other person at home, both have Medicare Parts A and B.
mismatches.heard: Rose's grandma renews her policy. She and Grandpa, the only other person at home, both have Medicare parts A and B.

mismatches.say: Memory trick: Medic-aid gets a little aid. Medic-are folks are allowed out, if the household is covered.

mismatches.say: The rhyme: Moving cars? P P I's not paying. Fences, buildings, properly parked cars in the mitten? P P I's paying, up to a million.

mismatches.say: Rosa's insurer says no: P P I won't pay for a moving car.

mismatches.say: Injury suits and out-of-state damage: residual liability.
